messages:
Maya P.: Hey team — quick question about the NAT GW egress behavior for the analytics VPC. We've got firewall rules that allow only the partner IPs, but those IPs are the NAT elastic IPs that AWS rotates. Is there a TTL for EIP reassignment that could break the allowlist? Also wondering if we should switch to a PrivateLink endpoint for the partner instead of NAT.

Jordan (ENG-SRE): Short answer: AWS doesn't rotate EIPs arbitrarily; EIPs only change if someone releases/allocates or if we recreate the NAT GW. Autoscaling NAT instances can change IPs though. If we're on managed NAT Gateway with a fixed EIP attached, it should be stable. :white_check_mark:

Sam T.: Are we using multiple AZ NATs? If so, there are multiple EIPs (one per AZ) — partner needs all of them on their allowlist. We had a break last month when one NAT got replaced and ops recreated it with a new EIP.

Maya P.: We're on per-AZ NATGW (3 EIPs). Partner only has two IPs allowed right now which explains the intermittent failures. Can we get a formal approval to share the third EIP with them? Also, will sharing these EIPs leak any logs with PII? Need security signoff.

Nikhil S.: For approval, we'll need: 1) list of EIPs, 2) minimal justification, 3) confirmation that only outbound traffic to partner is allowed (no inbound). Also check flow logs: we can redact user IDs in VPC Flow Logs at ingestion; we don't store full headers. I'll loop in @audit-bot for logging policy.

audit-bot: ACTION REQUIRED: Submit security request with template: /security-request template=egress-ip-share env=prod. Attach flow logs sample and intended TTL for the mapping. Link: https://redwood-internal/security-requests

Maya P.: Copying the EIPs here: 3.102.45.11, 3.102.45.12, 3.102.45.13. Justification: partner webhook ingestion for anonymized usage metrics; only port 443 outbound. I'll prepare the /security-request.

Jordan (ENG-SRE): config note — add these to the outbound SG on the partner's side and in our egress allowlist. Route tables unchanged. If you want to avoid EIP sharing, we can create a PrivateLink/Interface endpoint (no public EIP exposure) but that requires partner to accept an endpoint — heavier setup but more secure.

Sam T.: Ops question — if we promote to PrivateLink, we'll need cert verification and ~1 week lead time. Also expected infra cost: ~ $0.01/GB + setup time. If partner agrees, recommend PrivateLink for long-term.

Maya P.: Thanks. Next steps: I'll file the security-request, include flow log redacted sample, ask partner to add all 3 EIPs, and propose PrivateLink as longer-term. @Nikhil S. can you pre-approve redaction config? @Jordan (ENG-SRE) can you prep the route/SecurityGroup snippet we should send partner?

Jordan (ENG-SRE): Will prep SG + example curl test and drop in the ticket. Example curl: `curl -v --connect-to partner.example.com:443:3.102.45.11:443 https://partner.example.com/health` — use this to validate. :thumbsup:

Nikhil S.: I'll pre-check redaction; if logs only contain src/dst ip + bytes, it's fine. I'll reply in the ticket today. If policy needs change, we'll route to risk committee.

Maya P.: Great — closing loop here. I won't make a config change until security-request is approved. Thanks everyone. :pray:
